content.title: 'FROM': 11 Burning Questions We Need Answered In Season 4
content.text: The MGM horror series FROM is a dark, gory descent into the paranormal, steeped in mystery. Centered on a group of people trapped within a small town, the show’s lore is deep and foreboding, with new questions piling up with each episode. Led by Sheriff Boyd Stevens (Harold Perrineau), the handful of residents stranded in the unnamed town cannot escape and are hunted each night by shadowy creatures that favor sadistic kills over quick deaths, often torturing their victims to inflict maximum trauma on those left behind. With Season 4 on the horizon, there are still plenty of lingering mysteries from Season 3 that demand answers, from the true nature of the town itself to the forces orchestrating its endless cycle of fear. Of all the questions surrounding the cursed town and its trapped residents, here are nine of the biggest that fans hope will be answered in Season 4. Warning: Spoilers for Season 3 of FROM ahead. FROM, Season 4 premiere, Sunday, April 19 at 9/8c, MGM+ MGM+ 1. Is Jim dead? In the Season 3 finale, Jim Matthews (Eion Bailey) and his daughter Julie (Hannah Cheramy) come face to face with the “Man in the Yellow Suit,” a figure who seems to have a vested interest in keeping the secrets of the town a well-hidden secret. “Knowledge comes with a cost,” explains the Man in Yellow as he gets closer to the duo. Jim tells Julie to run as the man grabs him by the throat. “Your wife shouldn’t have dug that hole, Jim,” the man tells him, followed by him ripping out his throat. It does not bode well for Jim, for even if there was a way to get help, there are no doctors, no hospitals, and no surgeons in town. MGM+ 2. Who is the "Man in the Yellow Suit"? The Man in Yellow, or the Man in the Yellow Suit (Douglas E. Hughes), is a mysterious, antagonistic figure who appears to be toying with the unfortunate residents of the nearby town and their unusual, supernatural predicament. Unlike the other creatures, he can move about freely during the day. He was previously teased in Victor’s mother’s paintings, which depicted a malicious figure dressed in yellow. He seems to possess knowledge of the town’s lore and may be directly connected to the dark supernatural forces that keep its residents trapped. Some fan theories surrounding the Season 3 finale state that the Man in the Yellow Suit is believed to be the entity that promised the original residents of the town eternal life in exchange for sacrificing their children. MGM+ 3. Is Smiley really back? Fatima (Pegah Ghafoori) gives birth to a fleshy mass, which is immediately snatched away by the Woman in a Kimono. Boyd follows her into the tunnels, where he finds several of the town’s creatures standing in a circle around the “baby,” which is now rapidly growing. The mass continues to expand before eventually standing, revealing a smile that is all too familiar to viewers. It appears that the “baby” is the reincarnation of Smiley, one of the town’s more infamous creatures, who was killed by Boyd after he transferred his blood-borne worms to him by cutting his own hand and slashing Smiley’s throat. Though the humanoid bears a striking resemblance to Smiley (Jamie McGuire), it has yet to be confirmed that it is the same evil entity, though the implications are strong. Smiley is believed to be one of the original townspeople who sacrificed the children. MGM+ 4. Were Jade and Tabitha the only ones who are reincarnated? In the FROM Season 3 finale, Tabitha (Catalina Sandino Moreno) and Jade (David Alpay) are revealed to be reincarnations of individuals from the town’s past, specifically Miranda (Victor’s mother) and Christopher. According to the lore, they are consistently reincarnated into the town in an attempt to save the children from their fate, one that already occurred many years ago. They appear to be part of an ongoing cycle, returning again and again to try to free the children, a mission they have failed in previous lives. It is unknown whether they are the only ones who have been reincarnated with the mission to save the children, but given the nature of the town and its predilection for eternal cycles, that seems unlikely. MGM+ 5. What is the purpose of the town and its creatures? The town appears to be a living trap, meant to capture new people and make them its permanent residents, but not allowing them to leave. Any road taken will lead back to the town center. The town seems designed to break people mentally, and it forces survivors to face traumatic situations while preventing them from leaving. It also occasionally demands a sacrifice to be appeased. Furthermore, at night, the residents must hide from creatures who wander the town. These are human-looking monsters who feed on despair and fear, often engaging in psychological torment of the residents. The “curse” seems to act as a trap that brings people, buildings, and items from the real world into a pocket dimension, rather than a force that prevents the physical construction of structures It is believed that the murderous creatures are former humans who once sacrificed their own children for immortality, but are now cursed to live in the town forever and feed its needs. MGM+ 6. Who promised the original cursed residents eternal life? The original cursed residents of the town sacrificed their children in exchange for eternal life, and becoming monsters that live forever to haunt and hunt the town is their curse. According to the lore, the original residents were believed to have been tricked by the demon. While it is unknown who or what made this pact with the original townspeople, some fans believe it is the Man in Yellow. MGM+ 7. Who is the "Boy in White"? The Boy in White (Vox Smith) is a mysterious figure whose origins and backstory are unknown as of the beginning of Season 4. His fate and how he ended up as an undead entity in the town are unknown. Acting as a guide to certain characters, he appears as a young boy in clean clothing who is somehow connected to the “faraway tree.” He seems to appear when people are in danger. In Season 3, the Boy in White was responsible for pushing Tabitha out of a lighthouse window, a move thought to have killed her but actually allowed her to escape the town. He might be using the residents to help solve the mystery of the town or accomplish another goal. It is unknown if the Boy in White is benevolent. He appears to be friends with Victor. MGM+ 8. How do the talismans work? The talismans are rune-carved stones that create a protective barrier against the nocturnal creatures, preventing them from entering buildings. They only work when hung inside a structure, effectively keeping the monsters out. Discovered by Boyd in a cave in the forest, where they appear to have been left behind, the talismans seem to be ancient. Their magic has yet to be explained, and it remains unknown who created them. Chris Reardon/MGM+ Will Victor ever reveal everything he knows about the town? Victor Kavanaugh (Scott McCord) is the longest-tenured resident of the mysterious town in FROM, having been trapped there since childhood, when he arrived with his mother and sister. Deeply traumatized and emotionally stunted, Victor often behaves like a small child, but he appears to know far more about the town than he can fully communicate. He has knowledge of the Boy in White, the Faraway Trees, and the tunnels, often using his drawings to convey the horrors he has witnessed. Recently, Victor’s father, Henry (Robert Joy), arrived in town, reuniting with his son after many decades. He is attempting to help Victor through his trauma. Chris Reardon/MGM+ 10. What is the purpose of the bottle trees? Dubbed “Faraway Trees” by Victor, the bottle trees are ancient trees with hollow trunks that act as unpredictable teleportation devices, transporting people to different locations within the town’s vicinity. The exact total number of Faraway Trees is unknown, but Victor indicates there are “many” throughout the forest. Sometimes marked by hanging bottles, there is a connection to the former residents that has yet to be uncovered. Chris Reardon/MGM+ 11. Will the town's name ever be revealed? Unknown. Writers will probably keep the mystery going until the end of the series, and even then, fans might not get an answer. Until then, fans of the show call it Fromville.
